findings.title: CVE-2026-63292: Apache HTTP Server: mod_vhost_alias stack overflow
findings.summary_md: oss-security disclosure posted by Eric Covener for the Apache security team on October 1, 2026, rating CVE-2026-63292 as moderate. A stack-based buffer overflow in mod_vhost_alias in Apache HTTP Server through 2.4.68 lets a remote client cause denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code by sending a Host header exceeding 8192 bytes, when VirtualDocumentRoot uses a hostname format specifier and LimitRequestFieldSize is raised above the default. Credited to Hyojae Lee and Zhen Kong, reported to the security team on June 17, 2026, fixed in 2.4.x by r1938676 and shipped in the 2.4.69 release the same day.

findings.title: Changes with Apache 2.4.69 (httpd 2.4.x CHANGES, r1938652)
findings.summary_md: Apache source repository commit publishing release httpd-2.4.69, which records the 2.4.69 CHANGES entries and the 2.4.69 release date of October 1, 2026. The commit is the earliest machine-readable evidence that the October patch train shipped on October 1, 2026, ahead of the news coverage that followed.

findings.title: Apache HTTP Server 2.4 vulnerabilities (vendor advisory, 2.4.69 release entry)
findings.summary_md: The Apache HTTP Server Project security page records the 2.4.69 release on October 1, 2026 with 20 CVEs: 5 moderate and 15 low. Moderate items include CVE-2026-63292, the mod_vhost_alias stack overflow, CVE-2026-57941, a mod_http2 use-after-free via shared session bbtmp re-entrancy affecting 2.4.17 through 2.4.68, and CVE-2026-42528, a mod_dav shared lock overflow affecting 2.4.67 and earlier. The page also lists CVE-2026-119618, CVE-2026-106023 and CVE-2026-109163 as the three fixes in the later 2.4.71 release.

findings.title: harden vhost_alias (httpd 2.4.x, r1938676)
findings.summary_md: Source commit merged into the 2.4.x branch on September 29, 2026 that hardens mod_vhost_alias ahead of the 2.4.69 release, and is the change later identified as the fix for CVE-2026-63292. Its date shows the code fix predated the public advisory by two days and the story's first-seen timestamp by three days.

findings.title: Multiple Apache HTTP Server Vulnerabilities Could Enable Code Execution Attacks
findings.summary_md: Trade coverage of the Apache HTTP Server 2.4.69 release published October 2, 2026, stating that the Apache Software Foundation released 2.4.69 on October 1, 2026 to address flaws enabling code execution, server crashes, data leaks and authentication bypass. Reports the advisory lists 20 vulnerabilities: five rated moderate and 15 rated low. Published shortly before the story's first-seen timestamp.
